**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed)

The agreement contains no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation binding Sparkling, which sits at the playbook's **preferred** position.

What I checked:
- **§ 2 (Grant of License)** — the licence is expressly "non-transferable and non-exclusive"; no requirement to source only from Garman.
- **§ 3 (Restrictions on Use)** — limited to standard copying, sublicensing, reverse-engineering and scope-of-use restrictions; nothing barring us from procuring competing software or services from third parties.
- **§ 10 (Maintenance and Support)** and **§ 11 (Fees)** — no sole-source support language; maintenance is a renewable one-year term with no lock-in.
- **§ 19 (Non-Solicitation)** — mutual employee non-hire only, not exclusive dealing.
- Remaining "exclusive" hits are unrelated: exclusive remedy (§ 15), non-exclusive escrow licence (§ 16), non-exclusive jurisdiction (§ 20(h)).

No provision restricts our freedom to buy from other suppliers, so there is nothing to narrow or delete.
